boundary_rationale: A new woe-onset addresses a wholly different subject — Assyria, not the decree-writers of the preceding unit: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט (oshb:Isa.10.5, byte tier), “Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!” (web:Isa.10.5). The unit runs through Assyria's own boastful self-assessment and closes at the rhetorical question comparing Jerusalem to Samaria, הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי (oshb:Isa.10.11, byte tier), “shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?” (web:Isa.10.11), before a fresh temporal-response clause opens the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through the king's boast quotation that follows is rejected because a temporal-response clause opens a distinct divine reply rather than continuing Assyria's own self-description.

The quotation formula כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר (oshb:Isa.10.8, byte tier), “Aren’t all of my princes kings?” (web:Isa.10.8), separates the divine first-person speech of web:Isa.10.5-web:Isa.10.7 from the king's own quoted boast running web:Isa.10.8-web:Isa.10.11; the unit is held together across that internal frame because the boast is itself the content the divine word introduces, addressed to the same Assyrian figure in both halves, so the quotation is read as continuing the speech rather than opening a fresh unit. A ketiv/qere note also sits at web:Isa.10.6, staged as the doubled pair ולשימו וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ (oshb:Isa.10.6, byte tier); it was checked before slicing near that verse and is disclosed here without a content claim resting on either reading, matching the practice already followed elsewhere.

boundary_rationale: A temporal-response formula opens the divine reply to Assyria's arrogance: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי יְבַצַּ֤ע (oshb:Isa.10.12, byte tier), “Therefore it will happen that when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the willful proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the insolence of his arrogant looks.” (web:Isa.10.12). A further therefore-clause לָ֠כֵן (oshb:Isa.10.16, byte tier) restates the same sentence rather than opening a new addressee, and the unit closes with the forest stripped bare, “The remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, so that a child could write their number.” (web:Isa.10.19).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the two therefore-clauses at web:Isa.10.12 and web:Isa.10.16 as separate rows is rejected because the king's own quoted boast, opened by the quotation frame at oshb:Isa.10.13, sits between them, and the unity is argued over that quotation rather than over any shared addressee, since neither therefore-clause has one.
